papers.abstract: The merger of neighboring towns and villages has given Toyota City more semi-mountainous areas with scattering villages and more districts where public transport is not available. As a possible means of operation in such semi-mountainous areas, the city government conducted an experiment of the demand-responsive system with phone reservations, using what is called welfare bus services for travel support for the elderly. As a result, greater efficiency marked the operations to some extent, while meeting user needs. This paper reports on the outline of the experiment and some possible problems over future deployment. papers.title: Matching workers with jobs: how well is the New Zealand labour market doing?
papers.abstract: Since the trough of the 2008/09 recession, the unemployment rate has remained high. However, some other indicators suggest that there might be less downward pressure on wage and price inflation than the unemployment rate alone implies. We explore this apparent discrepancy by looking at the relationship between vacancies and the number of people unemployed (the Beveridge curve) and by estimating a measure of the effectiveness of the labour market at matching unemployed workers with vacancies. We suggest that both the Canterbury earthquakes and international migration flows may have contributed to an apparent decline in the matching efficiency in the labour market.

papers.abstract: Taller workers receive a wage premium. Net of differences in family background, the disparity is similar in magnitude to the race and gender gaps.
